transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-14
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Ben Carter (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Janelle Park (Medoria Head of ML), Tom Rivera (Medoria Infra), Priya Shah (Medoria Security)

Summary:
Quick scoping to align on POC success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks and whether Hosted / Dedicated / Private is the right deployment mode for Medoria's clinical summarization product. Action items and next steps captured at end.

Topics:
- Success criteria and SLOs
- Workload shape and sizing (RPS, token counts, concurrency)
- Benchmark plan (latency/cost/quality)
- Deployment decision drivers (data residency, encryption, throughput predictability)
- Timeline and stakeholders

Transcript:
[00:00] Ben Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side, I'm Ben, AE at Redwood, and Maya is our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Maya Singh: hi all, thanks for having us. we'll do a quick framing then dive into sizing — there's some slides but i think we'll keep it conversational.
[00:22] Janelle Park: thanks, ben, maya. i'm Janelle, lead on the clinical summarization project. goal is to roll out to a pilot of 50 clinicians in Q2 and production by Q3. main concerns are PHI handling, latency under 300ms tail for snippets, and predictable cost.
[00:40] Tom Rivera: infra here — we manage k8s clusters, want to understand network egress, VPC peering for private, and what Dedicated means for our sizing and budget.
[00:50] Priya Shah: security and compliance, quick note: SOC 2 plus need KMS integration, audit logs, and potential for on-prem in long term.
[01:05] Ben Carter: great, that's exactly what we expect to cover. first, can you share current workload shape? what are your expected request per second, average prompt and response token sizes?
[01:18] Janelle Park: for pilot, roughly 0.5 RPS across the pilot users but bursts up to 5 RPS when clinics start shift change. avg prompt tokens about 120, avg response tokens 300. under production we expect steady-state 10 RPS with peaks to 50 RPS, concurrency maybe 30.
[01:38] Maya Singh: okay that helps. so three vectors: latency target (95/99p), cost per 1k tokens, and data residency. For Hosted — fastest to get started, we handle everything, but for PHI you need to review data retention and BAA, and we have dedicated options too.
[01:55] Tom Rivera: the Dedicated option — does that mean our own GPU pool, like we reserve capacity? how isolated is it?
[02:05] Maya Singh: yes, Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity for your tenant. it's isolated, predictable throughput and can be deployed in a customer VPC with private connectivity in our Private offering. sometimes folks confuse Dedicated and Private: Dedicated is reserved capacity in Redwood's infra, Private is customer-managed control plane or on-prem.
[02:22] Janelle Park: so for PHI, Private on our VPC or on-prem makes us comfortable, but it adds ops overhead. want to understand quantifiable tradeoffs.
[02:32] Ben Carter: totally — that's the decision criteria we usually help teams map. quick checklist: 1) Data residency & compliance; 2) Throughput predictability and cost; 3) Latency SLOs and variability; 4) Ops overhead and timeline.
[02:45] Priya Shah: about KMS — we require CMEK key control and an HSM-backed option if possible. do you support that with Private?
[02:54] Maya Singh: yes, with Private you can bring-your-own-KMS and integrate an HSM. For Dedicated we offer KMS integration with customer keys in some regions, but it's more limited than fully private. we'll share the security matrix after this call.
[03:10] Tom Rivera: how do you run benchmarks? we'd like a bench that reflects our prompt distribution and include 95th pct latency.
[03:18] Maya Singh: we typically provide a benchmark harness — a script that can replay sampled prompts at target RPS under different concurrency shapes, and we measure latency, token-per-second throughput, and cost. we'll give you the harness and sample results for similar customers.
[03:30] Janelle Park: good. and model choice — we need medically-tuned output. do you recommend an open model or something redwood-verified? and how do you handle hallucinations/regressions in a POC?
[03:43] Ben Carter: we have curated model catalog and can recommend models with quality vs cost tradeoffs. for hallucination monitoring, we instrument evals against known cases and gating rules; for POC we usually include a small eval set and quality acceptance criteria (precision at x).
[03:56] Tom Rivera: cost question — hosted per-token pricing vs dedicated commitment — what's typical break-even?
[04:03] Maya Singh: depends on utilization. rough rule: if sustained throughput leads to >X tokens/month (we'll send the exact breakpoint in the worksheet), Dedicated tends to be cheaper. we provide a calculator; we'll fill it for your anticipated 10 RPS baseline.
[04:20] Janelle Park: timeline — we want pilot in Q2. how long for Dedicated or Private to be stood up?
[04:27] Ben Carter: Hosted: minutes to get started, we spin up API keys. Dedicated: typically 2-4 weeks for reserved capacity and config depending on region. Private (VPC) can be 4-8 weeks depending on network approvals and KMS setup; on-prem longer.
[04:40] Priya Shah: network compliance — do you support AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering for Private?
[04:46] Maya Singh: yes PrivateLink and VPC peering are supported; we'll include network requirements doc.
[04:52] [crosstalk] Janelle Park: how do we validate quality under the POC?
[04:58] Maya Singh: recommended steps — 1) agree on acceptance eval set (20-50 prompts); 2) run local benchmark for latency/cost; 3) run human-in-the-loop review for N outputs; 4) pass a quality gate (e.g., >=95% relevance and NO high-risk hallucinations on sampled cases).
[05:15] Tom Rivera: for the benchmark harness, what telemetry do you capture? we need token-level cost, per-request lat, and traces to link to our tracing system.
[05:24] Maya Singh: we capture per-request latency, token counts, and error rates; for Dedicated/Private we can instrument tracing hooks to send to your X-Ray/Prometheus. we'll provide a tracing integration guide.
[05:36] Ben Carter: i want to call out fallback policies — if you go Hosted and hit capacity or region outage, we can route to compatible model variants; Dedicated has SLAs and higher predictability.
[05:48] Janelle Park: ok security nuance: do you retain prompts? we need a BAA and explicit zero-retention for PHI in Hosted.
[05:59] Maya Singh: we have configurable retention. for PHI we recommend Private or Dedicated with retention disabled and BYOK. we'll escalate BAA specifics; legal will share terms.
[06:10] [00:06:10] Priya Shah: also need audit logs for all requests and key operations — is that a standard offering?
[06:16] Maya Singh: yes audit logs are standard for Dedicated/Private; Hosted has logs but retention windows differ.
[06:22] Ben Carter: next let's align on success criteria — Janelle, what's non-negotiable for the pilot?
[06:28] Janelle Park: pilot success: avg latency under 250ms, 95th under 400ms, no critical hallucination incidents across the eval set, cost under USD X per clinician per month (we'll provide their budget).
[06:40] Ben Carter: great. we'll use that to set benchmark thresholds. for POC scope we'll propose: 2-week benchmark run, one week of integration and security review, and 2-week pilot with 50 users.
[06:53] Tom Rivera: for the 2-week benchmark — do we run on Hosted first or Dedicated?
[06:58] Maya Singh: typically run initial bench on Hosted (fast) to validate model and prompts, then repeat on Dedicated or Private to measure delta. that gives you apples-to-apples.
[07:09] Janelle Park: what about quantization/throughput optimization — can you recommend approaches so we get lower cost but keep quality?
[07:16] Maya Singh: yes, Redwood Optimize suggests quant profiles per model and workload. for latency-sensitive flows we avoid aggressive quantization unless it's validated on the eval set. we'll include recommended config e.g., 8-bit quant for non-critical background tasks.
[07:31] Ben Carter: i'll summarize deliverables: pricing + Dedicated sizing worksheet, benchmark harness + sample scripts, security matrix and network reqs.
[07:40] Janelle Park: great. any blockers from our side? we need an internal legal review for BAA, and infra needs to provision a VPC peering window if we go Private.
[07:50] Priya Shah: i'll start the compliance review and send a list of required attestations.
[07:55] [00:07:55] Maya Singh: small note on telemetry: for measuring 95p we'll ask you to run the harness for 24-48 hours under target load to capture realistic tails.
[08:04] Tom Rivera: fine. also can you include estimated ops overhead for Private vs Dedicated? we need headcount estimates.
[08:11] Ben Carter: yes we'll include a rough ops estimate. Dedicated: low ops overhead; Private: higher ops commitment (network, KMS, upgrades).
[08:20] Janelle Park: final question — rollback strategy if model quality regresses in production?
[08:26] Maya Singh: we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to prior model variants. Redwood Console will show per-route metrics and quality regressions; we can set automated alerts and rollbacks.
[08:38] Ben Carter: ok last thing — timeline alignment: we'll aim to have the workbook and bench harness in your inbox by Jan 17, you provide usage and prompts by Jan 20, then we schedule the SE deep-dive week of Jan 26.
[08:52] Janelle Park: sounds good. thanks, everyone.
[08:56] Priya Shah: thanks.
[09:00] Ben Carter: thanks, we'll follow up with all artifacts.
